newsitem.title: USA: States sue Mazda over advertising.
newsitem.headline: States sue Mazda over advertising.

text.p: Missouri joined 13 states in filing separate lawsuits Monday against Mazda Motor of America Inc, saying that the auto manufacturer ran false and deceptive advertising about its auto leasing program.

The lawsuits allege that Mazda required consumers to pay up-front fees of up to $900 to get the advertised "zero down" or "penny down" lease. The up-front fees include a security deposit and the first month's lease, payment and in some cases a $450 acquisition fee.
Consumer laws require advertising terms, such as up-front fees, be legible and understandable to consumers.

"Mazda very prominently promoted the theme of nothing down or one penny down to lease their vehicles, when in truth, Mazda required payments totalling hundreds of dollars," Missouri Attorney General Jay Nixon said in a statement.
Other states filing lawsuits against Mazda included Minnesota, California, Connecticut, Arizona, Iowa, Massachusetts, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Maryland, Washington, Nevada, and Ohio.
Mazda is 33.4 percent-owned by Ford Motor Company, which earlier this year installed the first foreigner as president of the Japanese automaker.
